subject.title: fix(agents): protect provider auth exchange output by sensitivity, not input marker

question: Should the shared provider-auth boundary treat every non-empty exchange output as secret unless `isNonSecretApiKeyMarker` explicitly classifies it as public?
rationale: The code and live proof support this fail-safe default, but it changes the shared security contract for all current and future provider auth exchanges and therefore needs explicit security/auth ownership confirmation.

options.title: Approve output-sensitive protection
options.body: Adopt the PR’s fail-safe rule, refresh it against current main, and require providers to register any genuinely public output marker explicitly.

options.title: Require provider-declared output metadata
options.body: Pause this patch and design a stronger typed provider contract that declares each prepared-auth output’s sensitivity before changing shared behavior.

options.title: Limit the repair to Mantle
options.body: Protect only Mantle’s generated bearer now, accepting continued recurrence risk for future marker-to-credential exchanges.

recommendation.title: Approve output-sensitive protection
recommendation.body: Adopt the PR’s fail-safe rule, refresh it against current main, and require providers to register any genuinely public output marker explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sentinel-egress security model and are the strongest history-backed owner for confirming its intended default classification.
